# Prastara

> Prastara is a free, open-source (MIT) AI server written in Rust that runs on your own PC. It runs mixture-of-experts models bigger than the machine's RAM, serves OpenAI-, Anthropic-, Responses- and Gemini-compatible APIs, and includes a web app, browser and computer use, a model Workshop and clustering of your own machines. It was called am2Strata until version 0.2.0.

Key facts:
- Bigger than RAM: hot experts pinned in RAM, cold experts read from the SSD on demand. Measured: a 17.5 GB model (GLM-4.7-Flash) on a 16 GB Mac mini M4 at 2.5x llama.cpp's generation speed (8.9 vs 3.6 tokens per second), with no swap written.
- Platforms: Linux x64 and Arm, macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows x64 and Arm. Computer tab: Linux. Sandbox VM: Linux with KVM.
- Install: a one-line installer that checks SHA-256 and needs no admin rights.
- Coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Qwen Code, Aider, Goose and the Gemini CLI connect in one command.
- Privacy: models run on your hardware; nothing leaves your PC unless you send it. Cluster links use mutual TLS 1.3 with pinned certificates.
- Name: Prastara (प्रस्तर) is Sanskrit for a layer spread out, the oldest form of the word "strata".
